question: A community health worker is preparing a village-level antenatal education session on preventing intellectual disability. Which of the following postnatal causes of Intellectual Disability Disorder is most amenable to primary prevention through public health measures?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Trisomy 21 is a prenatal (chromosomal) cause, not a postnatal one, and cannot currently be prevented through public health measures — only detected prenatally by screening.

Correct. Congenital hypothyroidism is a preventable postnatal cause — universal newborn thyroid screening followed by early thyroxine replacement can prevent intellectual disability entirely. It is a key example of secondary prevention through the national newborn screening programme.
Incorrect. Fragile X is a genetic (X-linked trinucleotide repeat) cause identifiable prenatally but not preventable through postnatal public health measures.

Incorrect. While preterm birth prevention has a public health dimension, cerebral palsy from prematurity is a perinatal cause. Congenital hypothyroidism offers a more direct, proven postnatal intervention with newborn screening.

overallFeedback.feedback: Return to the aetiological classification: genetic → prenatal → perinatal → postnatal. Postnatal causes (infections, hypothyroidism, malnutrition, lead poisoning) are most amenable to public health prevention. Congenital hypothyroidism is the benchmark example.

Well applied. Congenital hypothyroidism is the classic example of a postnatal IDD cause that is completely preventable with early detection (newborn screening) — a high-yield point for both clinical practice and national health policy.
